audit_answers.Q1_reason: N4E-A already exposes backend-neutral exact Reader/Writer protocols and exact restoration. A legal physical adapter must persist the already-canonical envelope bytes without interpretation, mutation, synthesis, merge, selection, repair, or fallback. Every inventoried concrete backend currently interprets a different domain schema or performs forbidden semantics.
audit_answers.Q3_dependency_relationship: Durable physical availability is below durable authority loading. Exact binding_ref provisioning is independently below RuntimeCanonicalAuthorityBindingResolver. Production startup composition is the join of loaded authority repositories, an exact admitted binding_ref, resolver resolution, CanonicalSemanticAuthoritySource, Frames, and C03. Neither durable loading nor binding provisioning can substitute for the other.
audit_answers.Q4_earliest_ready_node: NONE; binding provisioning creation/admission/deployment-selection/transport owners and production sources are absent, so the earliest gate is an Owner architecture decision rather than implementation.

inventory_result.reason: No current concrete implementation provides arbitrary opaque bytes, exact immutable ref-addressed reads/writes, exact byte preservation, and fail-closed corruption behavior behind the N4E protocols.

physical_backend_decision.reason: N4E-A's Reader/Writer protocols isolate physical persistence from authority semantics. The next architecture gate is ownership and provisioning of the exact runtime binding_ref, not a PostgreSQL/SQLite/JSONL/filesystem/object-store/append-only choice.
physical_backend_decision.next_backend_neutral_step_after_owner_ga: Specify the exact governed binding lifecycle owners and exact explicit config transport, then implement/compose backend-neutral loading and provisioning independently. A concrete backend choice is required only when a production adapter must be deployed or its operational guarantees must be tested.
